v5: restoring from the first read, new labels, and the line + trees model¶

2026-10-25

The story in one paragraph. We carried out the four recommended steps. (1) The first read of the detector (ZEROFRAME) now restores NIRCam pixels directly where it is reliable. (2) The PSF fit that makes our labels now also uses these first reads, so it sees much more of each star's core. (3) The test is the fair brightness-band test, with junk and failed fits removed. (4) The model is a straight line plus trees. Two findings changed the plan on the way: the pixels touching a fully saturated core hold extra charge spilled from that core (discussion_20261025.ipynb), so their first read cannot be used directly; and a few dozen failed PSF fits had been dominating the errors on the brightest stars.

Words used here¶

word meaning
first read / ZEROFRAME the detector's first read, 10.7 s after reset; below saturation for many pixels that saturate in group 0, so it measures them
A-hard a pixel saturated even in its first read: no usable read at all
touching ring the 8 pixels around an A-hard pixel; they hold extra charge spilled from the full pixel
label the "answer" we train on: the pixel's flux from a PSF fit of its star
failed fit a star whose labels disagree with its measured first reads by more than x3 on most pixels: the PSF fit did not describe it (usually a blend or a star on bright nebulosity)
brightness bands, x2 ... x32 the fair test: train on fainter stars, test on stars 2, 4, ..., 32 times brighter
dex a factor on a log scale: 0.1 dex = x1.26, 0.3 dex = x2
bias / scatter the typical error / the spread of the errors (half the middle 68%)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

BLUE, ORANGE, AQUA, YELLOW = '#2a78d6', '#eb6834', '#1baf7a', '#eda100'   # categorical slots 1-4, fixed order
INK, MUTED, GREY = '#0b0b0b', '#52514e', '#b5b4ae'
plt.rcParams.update({'axes.spines.top': False, 'axes.spines.right': False, 'axes.grid': True, 'grid.color': '#e6e5e0',
                     'grid.linewidth': 0.6, 'axes.edgecolor': GREY, 'axes.labelcolor': INK, 'xtick.color': MUTED,
                     'ytick.color': MUTED, 'lines.linewidth': 2, 'font.size': 11, 'axes.titlesize': 12,
                     'axes.titleweight': 'bold', 'legend.frameon': False, 'figure.dpi': 110})
W = '/orange/adamginsburg/w51/TaehwaYoo/w51_sat_recover'
M5 = f'{W}/model_v5'
half_width = lambda s: (np.percentile(s, 84) - np.percentile(s, 16)) / 2

def end_labels(ax, items, gap=0.07, dx=1.1):
    # name each line at its right end (log2 x axis); labels pushed apart so they never overlap
    lo, hi = ax.get_ylim()
    items = sorted(items, key=lambda it: it[1])
    ys = [it[1] for it in items]
    for i in range(1, len(ys)):
        ys[i] = max(ys[i], ys[i - 1] + gap * (hi - lo))
    for (x, y, text), yl in zip(items, ys):
        ax.text(x * dx, yl, text, va='center', fontsize=10, color=INK)

1. What changed¶

step what where
restore from the first read NIRCam level-0 pixels whose first read is below saturation (A-soft, B, C) and that do not touch an A-hard pixel: first read, converted with the pipeline's own flat and calibration factor py/restore_zeroframe.py (new), zeroframe_flux in py/making_training_set.py
new labels (v5) the PSF fit uses those first reads (and those of level-1 pixels) as data instead of masking them; A-hard pixels and their touching ring stay masked py/making_training_set.py; 480 exposures in .../w51_sat_recover/v5/
clean training set and fair test drop 3x3 junk and failed fits; match stars within 1"; brightness-band test instead of "brightest 20%" py/assemble_training_set.py, py/train_model.py
model straight line (ridge) for the trend + trees (XGBoost, quantile loss) for the rest, with a 16-84% uncertainty band; plain XGBoost kept as the baseline py/train_model.py; results in .../w51_sat_recover/model_v5/

2. Which pixels the first read can restore¶

The figure counts NIRCam level-0 pixels (the pixels with no pipeline value at all) by how they are restored now.

In [2]:
lm = pd.read_csv(f'{M5}/report_data/level0_methods.csv').pivot(index='wave', columns='method', values='pixels')
order = [('first read', AQUA, '', 'first read, directly'), ('touching ring, core <= 2 px', AQUA, '..', 'touching ring, core of 1-2 A-hard px'),
         ('touching ring', ORANGE, '//', 'touching ring (spill): model'), ('A-hard', ORANGE, '', 'A-hard: model')]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 2.9))
left = np.zeros(len(lm))
for col, c, hatch, name in order:
    ax.barh(lm.index, lm[col], left=left, color=c, hatch=hatch, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2, label=name)
    for i, (l, v, tot) in enumerate(zip(left, lm[col], lm.sum(axis=1))):
        ax.text(l + v / 2, i, f'{v / tot:.0%}', ha='center', va='center', color=INK, fontsize=10,
                bbox=dict(fc='white', ec='none', alpha=0.8, pad=1))
    left += lm[col].values
ax.set_xlabel('NIRCam level-0 pixels (all fitted stars, 3x3 junk removed)'); ax.grid(axis='y', visible=False)
ax.legend(loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.38), ncol=4, fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()
lm.assign(total=lm.sum(axis=1))

method A-hard first read touching ring touching ring, core <= 2 px total
wave
long wave 10785 4932 14203 2417 32337
short wave 8840 3898 12891 3360 28989

Reading it. Only about 14% of NIRCam level-0 pixels are restored directly by the first read, much less than the "three quarters" estimated before. The reason: most A-soft, B and C pixels sit right next to an A-hard core, and those touching pixels hold extra charge spilled from the full core (next figure). They go to the model instead, together with the A-hard pixels.

The touching rings of small cores (1-2 A-hard pixels, dotted) show no measurable spill. Restoring them directly too would raise the direct share to about 24% (decision 1 below).

2.1 Why the touching ring is left out¶

For pixels touching an A-hard core: the v5 label (from a PSF fit that did not use these pixels) against their first read, grouped by the size of the A-hard core. A value of 1 means agreement.

In [3]:
rc = pd.read_csv(f'{M5}/report_data/ring_core.csv')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.6))
cores = ['1-2', '3-5', '6-10', '11-20', '21-50', '>50']
for (w, g), c, mk in zip(rc.groupby('wave'), [ORANGE, BLUE], ['s', 'o']):
    g = g.set_index('core').reindex(cores)
    ax.plot(np.arange(6), 10 ** g.median_dex, marker=mk, color=c, ms=8, label=w)
ax.axhline(1, color=INK, lw=1)

2.2 Is the first read itself right?¶

Level-1 pixels have both a first read and a pipeline value (from their one unsaturated group), so they check the conversion of the first read to MJy/sr.

In [4]:
t = Table.read(f'{M5}/training_v5.fits')
T = pd.DataFrame({c: np.asarray(t[c]).astype(float) for c in ['sat_level', 'cal_value', 'zeroframe_flux', 'zeroframe_rate', 'label']})
T['inst'] = [v.decode() if isinstance(v, bytes) else v for v in t['inst']]
T['filter'] = [v.decode() if isinstance(v, bytes) else v for v in t['filter']]
l1 = T[(T.inst == 'NIRCam') & (T.sat_level == 1) & (T.cal_value > 0) & (T.zeroframe_flux > 0)].copy()
l1['r'] = np.log10(l1.zeroframe_flux / l1.cal_value)
l1['dn'] = l1.zeroframe_rate * 10.737
l1['wave'] = np.where(l1['filter'].str[1:4].astype(int) > 250, 'long wave', 'short wave')
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))
lo, hi = np.percentile(np.log10(l1.cal_value), [0.5, 99.5])
axes[0].hexbin(np.log10(l1.cal_value), np.log10(l1.zeroframe_flux), gridsize=60, bins='log', cmap='Blues', mincnt=1, extent=(lo, hi, lo, hi))
axes[0].plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], '--', color=INK, lw=1)
axes[0].set_xlabel('pipeline value (log10 MJy/sr)'); axes[0].set_ylabel('first read (log10 MJy/sr)')
axes[0].set_title(f'Level-1 pixels: median ratio {10 ** l1.r.median():.3f}, scatter {half_width(l1.r):.3f} dex')
edges = [100, 300, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000]
for (w, g), c, mk in zip(l1.groupby('wave'), [ORANGE, BLUE], ['s', 'o']):
    s = g.groupby(pd.cut(g.dn, edges), observed=True).r.median()
    axes[1].plot([iv.mid for iv in s.index], 100 * (10 ** s - 1), marker=mk, color=c, ms=8, label=w)
axes[1].axhline(0, color=INK, lw=1); axes[1].set_xscale('log')
axes[1].set_xlabel('signal in the first read (DN)'); axes[1].set_ylabel('first read / pipeline - 1 (%)')
axes[1].legend(); axes[1].set_title('Small offset at low signal')
plt.tight_layout()

Reading it. The first read agrees with the pipeline to about 2% (scatter about 0.02 dex). It runs 1-5% low below 3,000 DN and agrees within 1% above 10,000 DN, which points to a small constant offset (tens of DN, not corrected). Three quarters of the directly restored pixels are C pixels with 3,000-13,000 DN in their first read, where it runs about 1-2% low; the A-soft and B pixels (20,000-50,000 DN) agree within 1%.

3. The new labels (v5), checked on pixels left out of the fit¶

To check the labels without circularity, a separate run on 40 NIRCam exposures (4 per filter) left a random 30% of the first-read pixels out of the fit and compared the labels there with their first reads, for v4 labels (old fit) and v5 labels (new fit). A value of 0 means agreement.

In [5]:
hs = pd.read_csv(f'{W}/v5_holdout/holdout_summary.csv')
h = hs[hs.kind == 'heldout ZF pixels'].copy()
h = h[h.rows >= 50]
h['grp'] = h.wave.map({'SW': 'short wave', 'LW': 'long wave'}) + ', level ' + h.level.astype(int).astype(str) + ', ' + h.dist + ' from A-hard'
h['pbin'] = h.pbin.map({'(0.0, 0.8]': 'below 80%', '(0.8, 0.9]': '80-90%', '(0.9, 0.95]': '90-95%', '(0.95, 1.0]': 'top 5%'})
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.5))
labels = []
for i, (_, r) in enumerate(h.sort_values(['grp', 'pbin']).iterrows()):
    ax.plot([r.v4_bias, r.v5_bias], [i, i], color=GREY, lw=1.5, zorder=1)
    ax.scatter(r.v4_bias, i, color=ORANGE, s=60, zorder=2, marker='s')
    ax.scatter(r.v5_bias, i, color=BLUE, s=60, zorder=3)
    labels.append(f'{r.grp}, stars {r.pbin} ({r.rows:,} px)')
ax.axvline(0, color=INK, lw=1)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(len(labels)), labels, fontsize=9); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xlabel('label vs first read, median (dex)')
ax.legend(handles=[Line2D([], [], marker='s', ls='', color=ORANGE, ms=8, label='v4 labels'),
                   Line2D([], [], marker='o', ls='', color=BLUE, ms=8, label='v5 labels')], loc='lower right')
ax.set_title('Pixels left out of the fit: v5 labels are closer to the measured first read')
Out[5]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, 'Pixels left out of the fit: v5 labels are closer to the measured first read')

Reading it. On pixels the fit did not see, v5 labels are closer to the first read than v4 labels in almost every group (typically +0.01 to +0.03 dex, against +0.04 to +0.08 for v4).

One open point: total star fluxes. In the same run, the fitted total flux of stars between the 80th and 95th percentile of brightness is 0.04-0.06 dex (9-14%) lower in v5 than in v4; the brightest 5% and the fainter stars barely change. Two explanations fit: (a) v4 was pulled up by spilled charge in the level 2-4 pixels next to the core, which v5 balances with first reads taken before most spill happened; (b) a small first-read scale offset pulls v5 down. A test with dither repeatability and the narrow-band filters would tell them apart (step 4 below).

Failed fits. Stars whose labels disagree with their first reads by more than x3 on most pixels are dropped from training and testing: 68 star-exposures in v5 (114 in v4, so the new fit fails less often).

4. Line + trees against XGBoost, on the fair test¶

Trained on the faintest stars (band 0), tested on stars x2 ... x32 brighter. Solid lines: the cleaned test (junk and failed fits removed). Faint dashed lines: the same models before failed fits were removed.

In [6]:
m = pd.read_csv(f'{M5}/metrics_label.csv')
m0 = pd.read_csv(f'{M5}/first_try/metrics_label.csv')
def series(mm, inst, val, l0=None, model='band_pred'):
    b = mm[(mm.split == 'band') & (mm.pred == model) & (mm.inst == inst)]
    b = b[b.l0_type == l0] if l0 else b[(b.sat_level == 0)]
    b = b.sort_values('band')
    return 2.0 ** b.band.values, b[val].values
panels = [('NIRCam', None, 'NIRCam level 0'), ('NIRCam', 'A-hard', 'NIRCam A-hard'), ('MIRI', None, 'MIRI level 0')]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(17, 8.5), sharex=True)
for j, (inst, l0, title) in enumerate(panels):
    for i, val in enumerate(['bias_dex', 'scatter_dex']):
        ax = axes[i, j]
        items = []
        for model, name, c, st in [('band_pred', 'line + trees', AQUA, 'D-'), ('band_xgb', 'XGBoost', BLUE, 'o-')]:
            x, y = series(m, inst, val, l0, model)
            ax.plot(x, y, st, color=c, ms=7); items.append((x[-1], y[-1], name))
            x0, y0 = series(m0, inst, val, l0, model)
            ax.plot(x0, y0, '--', color=c, lw=1, alpha=0.6)
        if val == 'bias_dex':
            ax.axhline(0, color=INK, lw=1)
        ax.set_xscale('log', base=2); ax.set_xticks([2, 4, 8, 16, 32], ['x2', 'x4', 'x8', 'x16', 'x32']); ax.set_xlim(1.7, 75)
        end_labels(ax, items)
        if i == 0:
            ax.set_title(title)
        if j == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel({'bias_dex': 'bias (dex)', 'scatter_dex': 'scatter (dex)'}[val])
        if i == 1:
            ax.set_xlabel('how far beyond the training stars')
plt.tight_layout()

Reading it.

  • NIRCam level 0: on the cleaned test both models are nearly unbiased (within 0.05 dex); line + trees scatters less from x8 on (0.20 / 0.28 / 0.29 dex at x8 / x16 / x32, against 0.26 / 0.35 / 0.38 for XGBoost).
  • A-hard: line + trees stays unbiased (within 0.1 dex); XGBoost drifts low (-0.15 to -0.20 dex at x8-x32) and makes more impossible predictions (below the floor at x32: 45% of its predictions, none for line + trees).
  • MIRI level 0: both go low at x8 and beyond (2-7 stars per band); line + trees scatters much less (0.26-0.38 against 0.41-0.61 dex).
  • The dashed lines (failed fits still in): -0.2 to -0.3 dex for both models at x16-x32. Most of the earlier "extrapolation problem" was a handful of failed fits among the brightest stars. Caution: the failed-fit cut uses the first read, which is also one of the model's inputs, so the cleaned scores for the brightest bands may be somewhat optimistic; the truth lies between the solid and dashed lines.
  • For stars like the training stars (cross-validation), the two models are close: NIRCam level 0 0.112 vs 0.114 dex, MIRI level 0 0.222 vs 0.249 dex (table in the appendix).

One more thing to know. For A-soft and B pixels of the stars x8-x32 beyond the training range, line + trees predicts 0.04-0.23 dex above the labels, but close to their first reads (scatter 0.03-0.07 dex). These are mostly touching-ring pixels: the model follows the first read (which includes spilled charge), because the faint training stars have no spill to learn from. The photon-rate labels and the charge-like predictions disagree here by design (decision 3).

4.1 Is the uncertainty band right?¶

The model gives a 16-84% range for each pixel, widened so that it holds 68% of the labels in cross-validation. On the brightness bands it should hold 68% too.

In [7]:
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4.4))
for inst, c, mk in [('NIRCam', BLUE, 'o'), ('MIRI', ORANGE, 's')]:
    x, y = series(m, inst, 'cover68')
    ax.plot(x, 100 * y, mk + '-', color=c, ms=8, label=f'{inst} level 0')
ax.axhline(68, color=INK, lw=1); ax.text(2.05, 70, 'should be 68%', color=INK, fontsize=10)
ax.set_xscale('log', base=2); ax.set_xticks([2, 4, 8, 16, 32], ['x2', 'x4', 'x8', 'x16', 'x32'])
ax.set_ylim(0, 80); ax.set_ylabel('labels inside the 16-84% range (%)'); ax.set_xlabel('how far beyond the training stars')
ax.legend(loc='lower left'); ax.set_title('The uncertainty band is too narrow for brighter stars')
Out[7]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, 'The uncertainty band is too narrow for brighter stars')

Reading it. For stars like the training stars the band holds 65-67% (by construction). For brighter stars it holds only 25-46%: the model is more uncertain beyond its training range than it reports. The band needs to widen with the distance beyond the training range (decision 2).

5. Next steps and decisions for you¶

# what why effort
1 Also restore the touching rings of small A-hard cores (1-2 pixels) directly from the first read no measurable spill there (label / first read 0.97-0.99); raises the direct share from 14% to 24% code: an hour; a 2-hour v5 re-run
2 Widen the uncertainty band with the distance beyond the training range, calibrated on the brightness bands it now holds 25-46% instead of 68% for brighter stars hours
3 Decide what the touching ring should contain: the star's light (photon rate, consistent with the A-hard pixels and the star's total flux) or the charge the pixel recorded (consistent with what the pipeline does for unsaturated stars). Now the labels give light but the model's predictions follow the charge for the brightest stars. If light: add the A-hard core size as an explicit input to the line, so the spill correction can grow with it the two conventions differ by up to x2-3 next to the largest cores hours
4 Test the total-flux change (v5 is 9-14% fainter than v4 for stars at the 80th-95th percentile) with dither repeatability and the narrow-band filters tells whether v4 or v5 total fluxes are right hours
5 MIRI: try stpsf blurred by a small extra Gaussian per filter (discussion_20261025.ipynb) MIRI cores are broader than stpsf for small saturated areas a day
6 Produce restored images end to end (first read where valid, model elsewhere, with uncertainties) the goal of the project a day

Decisions: 1 (recommended: yes), 3 (my recommendation: light, so that the restored star keeps its total flux), and the order of 4-6.
